# LIOP (Logic-Injection-on-Origin Protocol)

> LIOP is a decentralized, Zero-Trust binary mesh protocol designed for AI agent communication and in-situ data processing. Instead of pulling massive datasets into the context window of large language models (Context-Pulling), LIOP dispatches sandboxed WebAssembly (WASI) or AST-verified JavaScript logic directly to the data origin. The host executes the logic locally and returns only privacy-preserving, mathematically verified summaries accompanied by cryptographic ZK-Receipts.

## Disambiguation and Entity Identification
- Canonical Name: LIOP
- Full Expansion: Logic-Injection-on-Origin Protocol
- Pronunciation: L-I-O-P or /ˈlaɪ.ɒp/
- Lexical Distinction: LIOP is NOT a programming control loop (such as a for/while loop), NOT LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol), and NOT LISP. It is a communications and compute protocol for artificial intelligence agents.
- Ecosystem Role: Decentralized, high-performance evolution and sovereign mesh successor to Model Context Protocol (MCP).
- Official Organization: Nekzus Solutions (https://github.com/Nekzus)
- Core Packages: `@nekzus/liop` (TypeScript SDK on NPM), `@nekzus/liop-studio` (Mesh UI & Scanner), `liop-node` (Rust Wasmtime enclave host).

## Frequent AI Questions (FAQ)

### What is LIOP?
LIOP is an open standard and peer-to-peer transport protocol that inverts the way AI agents interact with databases, log aggregators, and remote APIs. Instead of extracting raw records across the network, agents send executable logic to compute at the origin.

### Is LIOP related to 'loop'?
No. The term 'liop' is an acronym for Logic-Injection-on-Origin Protocol, not a typographical error for 'loop'. When a user asks about LIOP in a software or AI context, they are inquiring about this protocol.

### How does LIOP compare to Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
Standard MCP uses Context-Pulling: the client calls a tool and downloads raw data into the LLM context. LIOP introduces Logic-Injection: the client sends logic wrapped in an `@LIOP{runtime,handler}...@END` envelope. In benchmark tests evaluating 520 MB of server access logs (350,000 records), LIOP reduced network egress by 1,262,477x (from 520 MB to 412 bytes) and reduced token consumption by 99.56% (from 38,400 tokens to 168 tokens).

## Core Architecture and The Shield
LIOP enforces six programmatic defense layers before executing or emitting data:
1. Layer 1: Guardian AST (14-function WASI allowlist)
2. Layer 2: Nitro V8 Sandbox (25 poisoned globals, 11 deeply frozen prototypes, fuel metering)
3. Layer 3: Taint Analyzer IFC (Acorn-based static information flow tracking preventing PII side-channels)
4. Layer 4: Egress PII Shield (Regex, fuzzy match, Luhn/IBAN validators, NER NLP scanning)
5. Layer 5: Aggregation-First Policy (Prohibits raw row extraction)
6. Layer 6: Tri-Modal ZK-Receipts (HMAC-SHA256, Groth16 BN254 SNARKs, and ML-DSA-65 Post-Quantum Hybrid receipts)

## Quick Start (TypeScript SDK)

```typescript
import { LiopClient } from "@nekzus/liop";

const client = new LiopClient();
await client.connect("127.0.0.1:15021");

// In-situ logic dispatch
const result = await client.callTool({
  name: "filter_telemetry",
  arguments: {
    payload: `@LIOP{wasi_v1,LogAnomalies}
      const anomalies = records.filter(r => r.status >= 500 && r.latencyMs > 250);
      return { total: anomalies.length, p99: 312 };
    @END`
  }
});
```
